races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden

runners_data.name: Cyclone Code
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with two recent runs both at 6f on good ground, suggesting a drop to 5f could sharpen her finishing kick rather than blunt it; 63 days off may have her fresh, and she is well suited by the hot pace this field will generate.|

runners_data.name: Bit Of A Buzz
runners_data.note: The most experienced and consistent of the three front-runners — six runs, three placings, all at 5f — and Gary Carroll's booking for Gavin Cromwell (5 wins from 41 in 14 days) gives this short-priced market angle substance; she must fight for lead position early.|

runners_data.name: Scarlet Dream
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner who has raced twice at 6f and 7f on good and standard, so she is stepping down sharply in trip; only 10 days since her last run and two modest efforts to date make her vulnerable if she burns energy fighting for the lead.|

runners_data.name: Gus Mccrae
runners_data.note: Debut runner with style unknown but Colin Keane in the saddle is a top-level booking, and Noel Meade's operation rarely runs debutants without preparation; could be tactically versatile enough to slot wherever the pace allows.|

runners_data.name: Ahorey
runners_data.note: Unknown style on debut for W R Crawford, but the Seamie Heffernan booking suggests connections think she has a chance; without any form data her pace position will be decided by natural temperament from the gates.|

runners_data.name: Lion Of Fortune
runners_data.note: Has a flagged finishing fade, finished last of 11 on debut over 6f on good, and is stepping back to 5f; likely to press or lead early and is at real risk of being swallowed up when the pace tells in the last furlong.|

runners_data.name: Best Love
runners_data.note: Has raced four times and shaped with some promise — placed fourth twice at 5f — making her the most exposed prominent-style runner aside from Bit Of A Buzz; Declan McDonogh's experience could place her well if the front-runners implode.|

runners_data.name: Lady Romagna
runners_data.note: Debut runner with style unknown; W McCreery has had some recent activity (5 from 13 in 14 days) and Leigh Roche takes the ride, suggesting stable confidence, but there is no form basis to assess pace fitness.|

runners_data.name: Annie Batt
runners_data.note: Ran second on her second start at 5f on good — her best surface and trip — and Andrew Slattery both trains and rides, a combination that suggests a well-prepared horse with a clear plan; 53 days off is the only minor query.|

runners_data.name: Sadie Rose
runners_data.note: Two starts, both tailed off at 6f and both flagged as fading finishers; dropping to 5f with a tongue tie is a small positive, but neither run suggests she can compete at this level against experienced rival pace-setters.|

runners_data.name: Somethingaboutlove
runners_data.note: Unknown style debut runner; C W J Farrell's yard has limited recent strike rate and Rory Cleary takes a routine booking; no form data makes assessment purely speculative, and she is likely to find this competitive opener tough.|

races.paceDynamic: Scarlet Dream, Lion Of Fortune, and Bit Of A Buzz are all confirmed front-runners over this 5f trip at Navan, guaranteeing a hot pace from the first stride on good ground. Scarlet Dream and Lion Of Fortune will contest the lead aggressively, with Bit Of A Buzz — the only one of the three with proven proximity at 5f — likely to slot in behind if crowded early, though all three will push for the rail and burn energy in the opening furlong. This contested pace scenario over the minimum trip on a flat course is likely to see the leaders tied up or fading in the final 100 yards, consistent with Lion Of Fortune's flagged finishing fade and Sadie Rose's similar pattern. The race shape strongly favours hold-up and late-running profiles who can absorb the early carnage and pick up the pieces — notably Cyclone Code, Annie Batt, and any debutant with tactical patience.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out early and the pace is as fierce as the runner profiles suggest.
scenarios.body: The leaders set a scorching tempo, fade in the final furlong, and horses held up off the pace arrive with a powerful late run; this 5f sprint becomes a stamina-sapping test that rewards horses who conserve energy through the mid-section.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners check each other and the pace is surprisingly honest rather than brutal, leaving a prominent tracker to sprint clear.
scenarios.body: A horse tracking just behind the leaders — outside the scrimmage — avoids the fighting and quickens when the tempo steadies in the final two furlongs; prominent-style runners land in the ideal position without burning out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Strikes Fresh
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed debut runners (Gus Mccrae, Ahorey, Lady Romagna, Somethingaboutlove) produces a forward show with natural early ability.
scenarios.body: An unraced runner with unknown tactical style slots into a prominent berth behind the scrum and, free of baggage, quickens smartly when the pace collapses; Colin Keane on Gus Mccrae or Seamie Heffernan on Ahorey are the highest-profile threats.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Bit Of A Buzz settles into a controlled lead position and the other two front-runners tire first, leaving the most experienced of the trio to hold on.
scenarios.body: Bit Of A Buzz has the most solid 5f form of the pace-setters and has placed three times at this trip, giving her the fitness edge to sustain a gallop if rivals flame out around her; a small-field-pace scenario or brief early traffic could allow her to coast in front and not overspend.

watchPoints.text: Scarlet Dream, Lion Of Fortune, and Bit Of A Buzz will all push for the early lead — watch the first three strides for crowding and bumping that could unsettle any of them or the prominent runners immediately behind.

Lion Of Fortune carries a flagged finishing fade and was last on debut — if she fires from the front and ties up after two furlongs she becomes a significant obstacle for runners caught wide behind her.

Annie Batt ran a clear personal best (2nd, 5f, good) on her second start and returns here after 53 days; watch the market move — a market trim in the morning would signal stable confidence in a well-held hold-up profile that suits this pace map precisely.

Four debutants (Gus Mccrae, Ahorey, Lady Romagna, Somethingaboutlove) carry completely unknown tactical profiles — watch their position in the stalls and how quickly they jump, as a tardy start for any could compromise their race before it begins.

Bit Of A Buzz is the lone front-runner with genuine placed form at 5f — if she breaks cleanly and is allowed a solo lead by the others for even a furlong, she becomes the biggest on-pace danger and the scenario probabilities shift materially.

races.name: Navan Racecourse Handicap

runners_data.name: Prairie Girl
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong recent 5f form including a win and a place on Good ground, well suited by this trip and conditions; Terry Casey claims 7lbs and trainer Daniel Murphy has one winner from seven in the 14-day window, keeping her competitive at the top of the weights at 143lbs.
runners_data.comment: Prairie Girl won two of her last five starts, including back-to-back victories three and four starts back, but a disqualification and an unplaced effort cloud the profile, and she comes in rated 4 lb below her official mark from stall 11 carrying 143 lb.

runners_data.name: Amerilis
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who sets the entire pace dynamic; W J Lee aboard a horse with two recent Good-ground placings over 5f and the tongue-strap fitted, she can dictate entirely on her own terms here and her record of six runs on similar going (1W3P) makes her the key pace figure.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 18 on our figures and carrying 139 lb from stall 15, Amerilis is hard to fancy at these weights, though she does arrive on the back of a win last time and has experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Cuban Grey
runners_data.note: True hold-up type with a pair of Good-ground places over 5f in recent history; Luke McAteer rides for a trainer without a recent 14-day winner, and at 139lbs the weight is testing, but his finishing style could reward if any pace develops.
runners_data.comment: Cuban Grey shaped with promise when third two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, suggesting conditions pose no issues; carrying 139 lb from stall three, he looks well placed to build on that recent form after an 18-day break.

runners_data.name: Bad Boy Rizz
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse — his form includes wins and places on Good over 5f and 6f — and Colin Keane's presence lifts the profile significantly; 42 days off the track is a mild watch but the horse ran well fresh previously and the OR of 79 leaves room.

runners_data.name: Gotta Catch'em All
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up specialist whose Good-ground record is strong (2W5P from 15 runs) including recent wins over 6f; the step back to 5f is the key query, having operated mainly over 6f lately, and Siobhan Rutledge rides for a trainer whose 14-day form is flat.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner four starts back, Gotta Catch'em All has distance and going experience in his favour, though a ninth two starts back is a blot and the quick six-day turnaround is worth monitoring under 136 lb from stall two.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Cry
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with one win on Good ground and a place from 11 runs on similar going; the 7lb claimer Jessica O'Gorman rides, and a recent run six days ago means fitness is assured, though the OR of 77 and previous 6f form raise a distance question.
runners_data.comment: Sovereign Cry showed his quality with a win four starts back, but a ninth last time out and a quick six-day turnaround raise questions about his current form; he has experience over today's trip and going, though 136 lb from stall 12 will not make life easier.

runners_data.name: Dandyville
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran who races from hold-up, but recent form figures of 0000 across Good and Standish make this a difficult recommendation; Seamie Heffernan is a positive booking but the horse has struggled badly in similar conditions based on the last five outings.
runners_data.comment: Dandyville arrives here 18 days fresh, has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating of 82 marks him out as a serious threat at the head of the rankings — the chief concern is a winless streak across his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Shadow Of The Moon
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose natural style is to finish from the rear — flagged as fading in finishes and carrying a style-fit score of 0.93 — the 66 days since last run adds uncertainty; his one Good-ground win came over 5f so the conditions suit in principle, but the redistribution to midfield compromises his chance meaningfully.
runners_data.comment: Shadow Of The Moon showed a turn of foot when winning earlier in this five-race sequence, though she was unplaced last time out, sixty-six days off the track. She has run over today's trip and going before, and her speed rating of 86 sits well clear of her official rating of 74.

runners_data.name: Buddy Batt
runners_data.note: Rory Cleary partners this genuine hold-up type who is mapped to midfield precisely because there are more closers than the shape accommodates; 66 days off the course is the longest absence in the field, and while his stamina profile (5f Good placings) is fine, the style-fit concern at 0.92 tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Buddy Batt showed he can win at this level when scoring in his last five starts, though he has been unplaced last time out and returns after 66 days off; he has experience over today's trip and conditions, but a mark of 73 and 133 lb make life competitive from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Harry's Hill
runners_data.note: Prominent-style horse with an outstanding course-and-distance profile — 13 from 15 runs on Good ground over 5f including two wins — Paddy Harnett's 3lb claim is a bonus and the trainer's recent form is quiet but the horse's own record demands respect.
runners_data.comment: Harry's Hill arrives here in fair nick after winning last time out and finishing second two starts back, though a patchy recent record — with unplaced efforts also in the mix — keeps him from being an unconditional selection; he has run over today's trip and going, and returns after a 17-day break carrying 133 lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: Mint Man
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse displaced into midfield due to the crowded rear; Chris Hayes takes the ride and the horse has two wins on Good over 6f, though his most recent run was a flat last-of-eight effort and the drop to 5f may not suit his style — style-fit of 0.93 reflects the positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Mint Man won two starts back and was third three starts back, showing he can make the frame, but he comes here off an unplaced effort 11 days ago and has plenty to prove from stall 17 carrying 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Bold Optimist
runners_data.note: Ben Coen's booking lifts interest in this hold-up type who ran well placed on Good ground over 5f and 6f; Daniel McLoughlin has one winner from 16 recent runners and the horse has a place record on Good (1W4P from 15) — forced into midfield by the sheer volume of closers, limiting his chance.
runners_data.comment: Bold Optimist is winless in his last six starts, though a second three starts back and a third two starts back show he is competitive at this level; fit enough on an 11-day turnaround, he has distance and going experience to call upon, but 128 lb from stall six is no easy ask.

runners_data.name: Treasured Royal
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse trained by Gavin Cromwell, whose 14-day record is strong (5/41), though the OR of 68 and a recent blank (0) on Good over 6f are cautionary; Gary Carroll rides and the horse has Good-ground placing form, but the positional redistribution at style-fit 0.92 means the race shape doesn't genuinely suit.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Treasured Royal nonetheless rates considerably higher than her official mark of 68 suggests, and she has experience of both today's trip and going; the risk is that a latest unplaced effort leaves freshness to prove despite just 11 days between runs.

runners_data.name: Happy Henry
runners_data.note: Has two wins and five places on Good ground over 5f in 15 runs — the strongest Good-ground finishing record among the redistributed hold-up horses; Leigh Roche partners and William McCreery's 14-day figures (5/13) are noteworthy, though the horse must find space through a large field from a position that isn't his natural one.
runners_data.comment: Happy Henry arrives on the back of a ninth last time out, and though he won three starts back, he ranks bottom of the field on our figures, making him very hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and distance.

runners_data.name: Beach Barbie
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with all recent runs on Standish — no Good-ground form in the last five starts — so the conditions are an unknown; James Ryan rides for Edward Lynam, whose 14-day form is quiet, and the style-fit of 0.90 (lowest in the field) reflects genuine positional compromise in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Beach Barbie faces a stiff task, though a third last time out offers slim encouragement and she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Gonna Be Golden
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner who has yet to win on Good ground from nine tries (0W0P), though he has placed on Soft; Robert Whearty partners for A Oliver in a trainer whose 14-day record is poor (0/14), and while the style suits tracking Amerilis, the form in these conditions is a real concern.
runners_data.comment: Gonna Be Golden has struggled badly for consistency, with two sixths, two unplaced efforts and an unseat in her last six starts and yet to win in recent form, leaving her hard to fancy from stall 18 off a mark of 64; experience over today's trip and going is the one modest tick in her favour.

runners_data.name: Cashel Blue
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse shifted into midfield by the crowded rear, with a win and two places on Good over 5f from seven runs — the form figures suggest ability in these conditions; Reese Holohan claims 7lbs and the horse ran just 11 days ago, so fitness is fine, but the style-fit of 0.92 means the race is unlikely to play to his strengths.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well towards the foot of the field on our figures, Cashel Blue has been largely out of the frame in recent starts, with only a single win to show in her last six, and an unplaced effort last time a concern, though she has experience of today's trip and going and returns fit on an 11-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Alnofoor
runners_data.note: Prominent-style eight-year-old who has two wins on Soft/Heavy ground but no Good-ground wins from five tries; the 82-day absence is the longest in the field and Andrew Slattery rides for Claire O'Connell, whose recent 14-day record shows no winners — significant fitness and ground-suitability questions ahead of this return.
runners_data.comment: Alnofoor has been off the track for 82 days and, ranked 15 of 18 on our figures, faces a stiff ask here, with an eighth last time out the most recent evidence; he has run over today's trip and going before, and back-to-back wins three and four starts ago show he can find the form on a good day.

races.paceDynamic: Amerilis is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner 5f handicap and, with no other natural leader to challenge her, W J Lee can dictate a controlled, measured gallop from the outside of the front rank. Prairie Girl, Harry's Hill, and Gonna Be Golden will push forward to track her prominently, creating a competitive but not suicidal early tempo on Good turf. The field is laden with hold-up types — Shadow Of The Moon, Buddy Batt, Mint Man, Bold Optimist, Treasured Royal, Happy Henry, Beach Barbie, Cashel Blue, and others are all genuine come-from-behind horses redistributed into midfield on the map because there is simply no space for them all to settle at the back of a field this large, meaning several will race closer than ideal and compromise their late runs. The race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or in a close-tracking position just off the steady pace, as the absence of genuine head-to-head pace pressure from the front means the lead group are unlikely to be cooked before the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Amerilis Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Amerilis leads uncontested at a sustainable tempo and the race is won from the front two or three positions.
scenarios.body: Amerilis dictates on her own terms and the moderate gallop means prominent trackers like Prairie Girl and Harry's Hill — both with strong 5f Good-ground form — arrive at the business end full of running. With hold-up horses unable to make up significant ground off a controlled pace, the race is decided between the early possessors.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flyer Defies Crowd
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly faster than expected and a genuine late runner times their run to perfection through a tiring field.
scenarios.body: A higher-than-expected tempo, driven by all three prominent types (Prairie Girl, Harry's Hill, Gonna Be Golden) pushing Amerilis along, would create enough of a pace to allow a well-positioned late mover to pick up ground near the rail. Bad Boy Rizz and Cuban Grey, both true hold-up types with strong 5f Good-ground credentials, would be the primary beneficiaries if they thread through in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up horses that are forced into midfield positions manage to find clear running and generate late momentum.
scenarios.body: Horses like Happy Henry and Bold Optimist, both owners of genuine finishing kicks on Good ground over 5f and forced wide in a big field, could produce a strong late burst if they get an unobstructed passage inside the final furlong. Their true styles are compromised by the race shape, but their Good-ground records and class relative to OR suggest they are capable of running above their mapped role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Amerilis is pressured into a fast early pace and the entire prominent group ties up in the final furlong, handing the race to a fresh-legged outsider.
scenarios.body: A scenario where all front-side horses have burned their fuel sets up a rare opportunity for a horse like Gotta Catch'em All or Sovereign Cry, who carry strong recent winning form over 6f on Good and may get the run of the race down the outside. This is the least likely outcome given Amerilis's ability to control tempo unchallenged, but the sheer volume of prominent types makes implosion at least a marginal risk.

watchPoints.text: Amerilis (W J Lee) controls the tempo entirely without a rival pace-setter — if she bowls along unchallenged, she could be very hard to peg back from the front and the entire race shape hinges on her staying power.

Harry's Hill (Paddy Harnett, 3lb claim) has a 13-from-15 record on Good ground over this exact course and distance — his prominent style suits the anticipated pace shape perfectly and he must be respected despite quiet stable form.

The sheer volume of hold-up horses forced closer to midfield — Shadow Of The Moon, Buddy Batt, Mint Man, Bold Optimist, Happy Henry, and others — means traffic and interference in the final two furlongs is a significant risk in an 18-runner field; watch for horses finding trouble in running.

Bad Boy Rizz (Colin Keane) represents the biggest jockey upgrade in the field and is the most likely beneficiary if any pace develops from the prominent trio of Prairie Girl, Harry's Hill, and Gonna Be Golden pressing Amerilis — his Good-ground hold-up record makes him the standout closer if the tempo lifts.

Alnofoor returns after 82 days off for a trainer without recent winners — monitor the market for any drifting in the show that would confirm stable confidence is not high heading into this first run back.

races.name: Kilberry (Q.R.) Handicap

runners_data.name: Murat
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has won twice over similar trips on Good ground recently; Peter Lawlor yard in modest form (0/5 in 14 days) but Murat himself arrives on a retrieval run after a win 12 days ago and will push hard for the lead against Miss Gitana.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a short head into second last time out and a winner two starts back, Murat arrives here in excellent recent form on a quick 12-day turnaround, with experience over today's trip and going; the 174 lb burden is the one query, but his rating of 91 marks him as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: The Mediator
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner (1/40 in 14 days is volume-driven) arrives just 4 days after his last run, which is quick, but he has a strong placed record on Good ground and will travel prominently, which is the ideal profile for this race shape.
runners_data.comment: The Mediator has shown consistent placing ability in recent starts, and his experience over today's trip and going is a clear plus at a weight of 168 lb; however, winless in his last five and returning just four days after his latest outing, the trainer's dire 3% strike rate over the past fortnight is the significant concern.

runners_data.name: Whimsy
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator returning from a 124-day absence, which is a significant freshness flag in a large field; has placed on Good ground at 2m trips but the long layoff and pure hold-up style make it hard to see her getting into this from off a genuinely run pace.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts, Whimsy has run over today's trip and going and her rating of 82 marks her as a genuine danger, yet winless in her last four and returning after 124 days off, the fitness query is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Black Heather
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose Good-ground record shows four placed efforts in five Good-ground runs but his finishing positions have been weakening (12th, 4th, 4th recently); the crowded rear in this field amplifies his positional risk.
runners_data.comment: Black Heather arrives here fourth two starts back and third four starts back, yet to win in recent starts, though our rating of 89 ranks him second of 17 and he has experience over today's trip and going; the main risk is that unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Not Just Any Eagle
runners_data.note: Amateur ridden hold-up type who has placed at this trip on Good ground; his two most recent placed efforts came at 2m and 1m7f on Good, but in a 17-runner field he needs a clear run that is far from guaranteed from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Placed in two of his last three starts, Not Just Any Eagle arrives here 27 days fresh and has experience of today's trip and conditions, yet he remains winless in recent starts and a testing 165 lb burden under his current mark of 75 makes a step forward harder to predict.

runners_data.name: Friary Road
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse with a tongue-tie and two Good-ground wins at this trip profile; his placed record is strong but he is racing out of his natural role given the congestion at the rear, which the redistribution flag captures.
runners_data.comment: Friary Road has run over today's trip and going before and arrives here on the back of a placed effort last time out, yet he remains winless in his last five starts and the 163 lb burden is a significant ask for a gelding rated 73 officially.

runners_data.name: Timurshah
runners_data.note: Remarkably impressive form — four wins from four runs between 2m and 2m2f on Good ground — but his yard has made zero entries in the past 14 days and he has been off 31 days; if he turns up fit, his Good-ground pace figures are the strongest in the field and a pace collapse would suit him perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Timurshah nevertheless shows a small uptick in our rating over his official mark and has experience on today's going, though a run of finishes drifting from fifth to seventh suggests he is struggling to find improvement at this level.

runners_data.name: Jerandme
runners_data.note: Veteran 12-year-old hold-up performer who knows his job and is likely to get his preferred position despite the crowded rear; his form over 2m+ on Good/Standard is modest (no win in recent starts) but the experience helps him find daylight.
runners_data.comment: Jerandme has run over today's trip and going before, but is yet to score in his last five starts and returns after a 111-day absence, which tempers confidence; third two starts back offers mild encouragement for a gelding carrying 162 lb into a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Sequoiaspirit
runners_data.note: True hold-up operator with a sole Good-ground win over 2m+, but his best efforts have come on Soft; ridden by an apprentice, he is squeezed toward midfield by the weight of hold-up types in this field and his Good-ground form makes him a step below the principals here.
runners_data.comment: Sequoiaspirit has been knocking on the door with back-to-back thirds and a second three starts back, though he remains yet to win in recent starts; he has run over today's trip and going, but a hefty 162 lb is the challenge he must overcome.

runners_data.name: Day Trader
runners_data.note: A J Martin runner who has struggled at this trip recently (14th and 16th in his two Standard-ground runs), though he did place on Soft over 1m4f; pushed into a midfield slot by the redistribution, he is genuinely out of his comfort zone racing without his natural hold-up position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Day Trader does at least bring distance experience and a recent second to the table, though two unplaced efforts since that run and a hefty 161 lb to carry make further progress a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Miss Gitana
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a tongue-tie and excellent consistency on Good ground (15/15 Good-ground runs); she will contest the lead with Murat vigorously, and whether she fades or sustains is the key swing factor for multiple scenarios.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 14 of 17 on our figures, Miss Gitana is hard to fancy at the weights carrying 156 lb, though second last time out and a return to today's distance and going at least offers some familiar conditions.

runners_data.name: Liberated Light
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie horse with a win over 2m on Good ground in his recent form; though a hold-up type by nature, his course form and headgear make him one of the sounder each-way cases if he can get into a workable position from midfield.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Liberated Light at least brings distance and going experience to the table, and a speed rating of 80 offers some encouragement; however, 155 lb is a stern ask for a horse rated 65 officially, and consistent mid-pack finishes suggest a win remains elusive.

runners_data.name: Rich Belief
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a win over 2m1f on Good ground and a placed effort over 2m4f; the 7-day turnaround is notably quick and he carries a tongue-tie, but his natural style is compromised by the sheer volume of hold-up horses in this field.

runners_data.name: Jurality
runners_data.note: Form figures show wins at shorter distances (1m5f-1m6f on Good) rather than this 2m trip; mapped to midfield due to redistribution, the step up in distance combined with the style fit discount makes this a harder task than the OR of 60 suggests.
runners_data.comment: Jurality has finished fifth, eighth and fifth in his last three starts, making him hard to fancy as the lowest-rated runner in the field, though he has experience over today's trip and going and returns on a quick 12-day turnaround suggesting he is fit.

runners_data.name: Cala Gracioneta
runners_data.note: 4-year-old flagged for fading in the finish, which is a serious concern in a 2m race; the form shows two second-place finishes over 1m6f-1m4f on Good but the stamina question over this trip is underscored by the finishing fade pattern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 15 of 17 on our figures, Cala Gracioneta is hard to fancy off 149 lb, though she does return quickly six days after a second last time out and has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Young Churchill
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent form includes a sole top-three finish at 1m4f on Good; his redistribution into midfield makes this a positional compromise and his 28-day layoff combined with limited 2m form makes him an outsider interest at best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 13 of 17 on our figures, Young Churchill is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a third three starts back offers a crumb of comfort; 149 lb is a tough burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Slowdownbarney
runners_data.note: Prominent rider in a field of hold-up horses — a relative rarity here — with tongue-tie and blinkers; his form is moderate (no wins or places in 15 Good-ground runs) but his natural prominent style means he gets a clear run in the ideal slot for this race shape without fighting for position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 16 of 17 on our figures, Slowdownbarney has shown little to inspire confidence, with a run of seventh, sixth, and fifth suggesting modest progression at best; experience over today's trip and going, plus 27 days of freshening, are the slim positives here.

races.paceDynamic: Murat and Miss Gitana are the two confirmed front-runners in a 17-runner field over 2m on Good ground at Navan, and both will want to lead — Murat has led in recent wins over similar trips and Miss Gitana's form shows a consistent front-running pattern with a tongue-tie. With two genuine pace-setters contesting the lead, an honest, even gallop is the most likely outcome rather than a suicidal burn-up, meaning the race will be run at a rhythm that keeps the field compressed through the middle stages before stretching out from 3f out. The field holds substantially more hold-up types than can occupy the rear — Sequoiaspirit, Jerandme, Day Trader, Liberated Light, Rich Belief, Jurality, Cala Gracioneta and Young Churchill are all true hold-up horses but several are mapped to midfield because the back of the field is simply overcrowded; those best placed to secure their natural position are Jerandme (veteran who knows his job) and Liberated Light (tongue-tie, course form). This race shape — a genuine, honest pace set by two front-runners over 2m on Good turf — strongly favours prominent racers who can travel just behind the pace without expending energy early, then sustain their effort through the final two furlongs; pure hold-up horses who are crowded out of position face a significant structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Murat and Miss Gitana trade an even gallop and the race is run at a true rhythm throughout.
scenarios.body: The two pace-setters drive a genuine gallop that stretches the field from early on, setting up a test of staying power over the final 3f; prominent racers who travel smoothly in the slipstream avoid the positional chaos in the rear and hit the straight full of running.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Murat shakes off Miss Gitana early and gets a soft lead, controlling the tempo on his own terms.
scenarios.body: Murat, who has won over similar trips on Good ground and is ridden by an amateur claiming jockey for a small yard in sharp form, dictates a well-judged gallop and simply never gives the hold-up horses time to close; his superior recent form over this course profile makes him the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Murat and Miss Gitana push each other hard early and both fade, leaving the door ajar for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: An overly contested early pace between the two leaders would see them weakening inside the final 2f, creating a rare opportunity for the hold-up horses who have managed to track closer than their natural style in a large field; Timurshah's strong pace figures on Good ground and Friary Road's consistent placed record make them the likeliest beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Shuffle, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes interference and traffic problems, with no runner able to land a telling blow.
scenarios.body: In a 17-runner field over 2m, a compressed midfield pack can result in multiple horses being checked or switched in the straight, flattening the finishing order and delivering a messy result; horses with the widest draw advantage or quickest tactical response — notably The Mediator or Slowdownbarney — might steal a march on rivals still sorting themselves.

watchPoints.text: Murat and Miss Gitana — watch how aggressively they contest the lead in the first 4f, as a fierce duel between the two will fundamentally alter the race shape and dramatically increase the probability of a late surge from further back.

Timurshah — his four-from-four winning record on Good ground at this trip is exceptional but he has been off 31 days and his yard has no recent runners; if he shows any signs of rustiness in the parade ring, his chance is materially diminished.

The large field of 17 creates serious traffic risk in the early stages at Navan's tight bends — any hold-up horse caught wide or checked at a turn will lose many lengths and effectively forfeit their chance before the race develops.

Friary Road and Liberated Light — both carry tongue-ties and have placed on Good ground at this distance; if either secures a tracking position just behind the lead pair rather than being buried in the hold-up pack, they become considerably more interesting in Scenario A or B.

Slowdownbarney — the only prominent-style horse outside the two confirmed front-runners, he will fill the seat directly behind the pace and if both Murat and Miss Gitana crack in the final 2f, he is structurally positioned to pick up the pieces without any positional traffic issues.

races.name: Book Your Hospitality Now For Navan Racing Festival Maiden

runners_data.name: Chapel Lane
runners_data.note: Placed twice over this trip on good ground, showing course-distance form, and wears a visor; by nature a hold-up horse but this pace-dominated field will likely push it forward of its comfort zone, tempering confidence in a big finish.

runners_data.name: Elusive Path
runners_data.note: Consistent placer in three runs for G M Lyons, handled good and soft, and Colin Keane in the saddle is a major upgrade — will want to make all and is a genuine pace-setter who must handle being pressed hard from the outset.

runners_data.name: Let's Smash It
runners_data.note: Unexpectedly drops back to a mile after running over 9-10f, suggesting connections feel it needs a stronger early tempo to showcase its stamina; has run well in two of four starts and Donagh O'Connor gives it a live chance if it settles after an early fight for the front.

runners_data.name: Resurgence
runners_data.note: OR of 120 towers above most rivals on official ratings, but 351 days off the track is a significant question mark; if fit enough after Mrs Harrington's preparation, the class is real and it has shown good form on good ground in both career starts.

runners_data.name: Storzando
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce (3lb claim) partners this hold-up type who has struggled for consistency, finishing 3rd once in four outings; the genuinely strong pace here means it will find itself racing more prominently than ideal, which has not previously unlocked its best.

runners_data.name: Testaverde
runners_data.note: Debut runner for John Joseph Murphy with Seamie Heffernan booked — that pairing alone demands attention; running style and going preference are unknown, but the trainer has a strong record with first-time starters and the jockey booking is high-profile.

runners_data.name: Time Whisperer
runners_data.note: Two runs both resulted in 7th or 8th on good ground over this exact trip, showing no improvement; hold-up style looks out of sync with today's strong pace, and Liam Cusack's yard has just one runner in the past 14 days.

runners_data.name: Emiza
runners_data.note: D K Weld's filly ran 2nd on debut at the Curragh on standard going and steps up to a mile, which the trainer handles well; prominent style is perfectly suited to today's fast pace and Chris Hayes provides an experienced tactical partnership.

runners_data.name: Pattyandselma
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Adrian McGuinness with Rory Cleary up, running style entirely unknown; the trainer has been in decent form over the 14-day window (3/24) and McGuinness occasionally springs debutants, though evidence is thin.

runners_data.name: Riyazanka
runners_data.note: J P Murtagh's stable send out a first-time runner with Ben Coen, one of Ireland's most in-form jockeys — a compelling booking; unknown style makes positional assessment impossible, but the yard's pedigree in bringing on maidens warrants close watching.

runners_data.name: The Blonde Lady
runners_data.note: Anthony Martin's filly showed very little on debut, finishing last of ten over 10f on good ground; the drop to a mile may help, but the hold-up style in a hot early pace with a history of fading is a poor combination.

runners_data.name: Whatsin The Stars
runners_data.note: Three consecutive last-place finishes on good ground over this distance, headgear of a hood deployed; the fade flag is consistent across all three runs, and even a true pace today is unlikely to produce a different result for Paul Flynn's filly.

runners_data.name: Wooloongabba
runners_data.note: Three starts, three finishes of 11th or worse, with Siobhan Rutledge taking over — the hold-up style has generated nothing against similar company and the fade flag is firmly attached; hard to construct a realistic case today.

runners_data.name: Xirivella
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's gelding finished 3rd on debut on good ground and wore a tongue-tie; prominent style suits the pace on offer and Adam Caffrey is a handy booking — the step up to a mile for a relaxed traveller could unlock improvement.

races.paceDynamic: Resurgence, Let's Smash It, and Elusive Path all want to lead, guaranteeing a strong early gallop over Navan's flat mile from the jump. With three genuine front-runners contesting for the same ground, the pace is unlikely to be controlled — it will be pressed from the outset, almost certainly pulling the race apart in the middle stages and stretching the field into a test of stamina rather than finishing speed. Chapel Lane and Storzando are true hold-up horses by nature but are mapped to midfield because the rear of the field is more congested than the positional map can reflect — neither is likely to achieve its natural rearward berth, which weakens the credibility of any deep-closing scenario. This race shape — a fast, truly-run mile — strongly favours horses with prominent or midfield tactical positions that can travel into the pace rather than needing to manufacture it from behind, rewarding genuine stamina and relaxed cruising speed over raw finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners fight each other for supremacy and sustain a fast, unrelenting gallop throughout
scenarios.body: The trio of Resurgence, Let's Smash It, and Elusive Path burn each other out, leaving the race open to horses travelling in behind who can pick up the pieces in the final furlong. Prominent types who settle just off the pace — Emiza and Xirivella — are ideally positioned to pounce as the pace-setters fade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Resurgence — highest OR at 120, long absence — shows class and outstays rivals after a strong pace
scenarios.body: Despite 351 days off, Resurgence carries the highest rating in the field and if fit enough to dominate from the front, the class edge could prove decisive on good ground. A horse that can control fractions after the early pressure subsides will benefit, and Resurgence's OR advantage is substantial over the rest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutants Blindside Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced unexposed runners — Testaverde, Riyazanka, or Pattyandselma — arrives with untapped ability to exploit a truly-run race
scenarios.body: A genuinely fast pace suits unexposed types who can travel comfortably in midfield without burning energy early, letting the race develop into their strengths. Seamie Heffernan on Testaverde and Ben Coen on Riyazanka are high-profile jockey bookings that suggest connections harbour serious expectations on debut.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically in the final two furlongs and genuine hold-up horses can sustain a run from off the pace
scenarios.body: This shape is the least likely given Chapel Lane and Storzando are unlikely to achieve true rearward positions in this pace-heavy field, compromising their ability to deliver the late burst their style requires. Even if a gap appears, the redistribution of hold-up horses toward midfield means the finishing surge would need to come from further forward than ideal.

watchPoints.text: Resurgence, Let's Smash It, and Elusive Path are all confirmed front-runners — watch for a contested, scrappy early pace that could burn out all three and leave the race wide open approaching the home turn.

Riyazanka (Ben Coen, J P Murtagh) and Testaverde (Seamie Heffernan, John Joseph Murphy) are debut runners with elite jockey bookings — both could be significantly ahead of their assessments and should not be dismissed.

Emiza and Xirivella are the prominent types best positioned to capitalise on a pace collapse — watch their positions at halfway to gauge if they are travelling within themselves as the front-runners come under pressure.

Chapel Lane and Storzando are unlikely to achieve their natural hold-up positions in this field — if either drifts further back than midfield early, their chance effectively dissolves given the pace-driven shape.

Resurgence's 351-day layoff is the key fitness unknown in the race — watch its early behaviour in the stalls and its position by the three-furlong mark to assess whether Mrs Harrington has it fully wound up for this return.

races.name: Navan Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Battle Borne
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for McKenna who fades in finishes (flagged), has struggled badly in similar going (3 places from 15 similar-ground runs, 0 wins), and hasn't run for 75 days — the finishing-line flag combined with a weak recent record makes this a very tough ask in a 20-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Battle Borne is winless in his last six starts, with his sole recent encouragement a second three starts back, though an eighth last time out and a 75-day break leave fitness to prove under 142 lb.

runners_data.name: Dinamine
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up specialist with a recent win over this exact course-and-distance combination on Good ground and a confident 17-day return; Joyce's claim aids the weight and the form string contains the most relevant recent evidence in the race.
runners_data.comment: Dinamine won three starts back but has been unplaced on both subsequent outings, and his our rating of 54 sits below his official mark, suggesting he faces a stiff ask off 141 lb; that said, he has run over today's distance and going and returns on a manageable 17-day break.

runners_data.name: Perfect Judgement
runners_data.note: Hold-up style horse who ran second over 10f on Good most recently and has solid placed form at the mile trip; Gavin Ryan is a strong booking but the horse has never won and needs a clear run through a packed field.
runners_data.comment: Perfect Judgement shaped with real promise when second last time out, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 68 ranks him second in this field; the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and must bounce back from an unplaced effort two runs ago.

runners_data.name: Land Of The Giants
runners_data.note: Listed as prominent but is identified as the confirmed sole front-runner here; McGuinness has 3 from 24 in the last 14 days and Caffrey's booking suits, but a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 suggests this may be at the boundary of its comfort zone on pace.
runners_data.comment: Land Of The Giants shaped with promise when third four starts back and again six starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going on a fair weight of 139 lb makes him a serious threat here; the risk is that he has been winless in his last six starts and must find a way to convert.

runners_data.name: Blue Orquidea
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old hold-up type for Hogan with only three career runs, two of which have come on Good going; the lack of experience in a 20-runner handicap is a significant concern against more battle-hardened rivals.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked 16 of 20 on our figures, Blue Orquidea faces a stiff task here, with a sixth last time out doing little to inspire confidence; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 21 days between runs suggests she is at least race-ready.

runners_data.name: Wild Berries
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse who fades at the finish (flagged) and whose best recent form of a seventh on soft/standard going suggests the step up in opposition in this field is daunting; Holohan's 7lb claim helps slightly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and drawn from stall 18, Wild Berries faces a stiff ask, though she returns after 27 days and has run over today's trip and going before; her rating of 68 marks her as the one to beat if she finally delivers.

runners_data.name: Concaire
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a second place on Good at 7f but most form at shorter trips; runs off a hurdle headgear flag (hg:h) which is worth noting, and Lee takes the ride, though 75 days off and the step to a full mile in a big field is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Concaire has been winless in his last six starts, though a second two starts back shows there is ability to coax out; at 75 days between runs and 135 lb to carry, he faces a stiff ask, but he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Giselles Defence
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose entire career has been run over much longer trips (7f to 13f), mostly on soft or heavy; shuffled into midfield on the map but its true inclination is to race well off the pace — style fit is discounted at 0.91.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Giselles Defence steps up from an official mark of 53 carrying 135 lb from stall 17, with experience over today's trip and going at least offering some footing; a fifth last time out shows he can get involved, but the overall profile makes him a hard sell against stronger contenders.

runners_data.name: Virgil Tibbs
runners_data.note: True hold-up type across all five recent runs, never closer than seventh in five outings on Good ground this season; the 62-day absence adds doubt, and with a style fit of 0.90 its chance in this shape is materially reduced.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Virgil Tibbs has been consistently mid-to-rear, and 62 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and conditions before, though his official mark of 53 suggests he faces a stiff task from stall nine carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Dress Dance
runners_data.note: A 106-day absence is the first concern, followed by a fading-in-finish flag and a record of three consecutive double-figure finishes; Lavery's horse is a hold-up type placed in midfield on the map by necessity, and its profile does not suit a pace-controlled race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and without a top-five finish in three of those, Dress Dance faces a stiff ask from stall 20 carrying 134 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a break of 106 days could bring freshness back to the equation.

runners_data.name: Whosethebestboy
runners_data.note: Heffernan's mount has not run for 107 days and its entire form profile is over 10f to 13f — a mile handicap with 20 runners is a very different test, and the fading flag plus out-of-role placement together reduce confidence sharply.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and not seen out for 107 days, Whosethebestboy arrives here needing to find his best form on return, though he has experience of today's going and our rating of 60 gives him solid claims; the layoff is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Chou Chou
runners_data.note: Colin Keane's mount placed fourth last time at 10f on Good, which is the most encouraging recent data point; however it is a natural hold-up horse racing over a shorter-than-preferred trip and its style fit (0.91) reflects how compressed it will be in this field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Chou Chou does at least bring distance and going experience to the table and a fourth last time out hints at returning form, though a stiff 131 lb from stall 12 makes progress difficult.

runners_data.name: Zephron
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type who has not finished better than seventh in five consecutive runs, all on soft or heavy going — Good ground is a concern (sim-going: 7 from 15), the fading flag applies, and the race shape does not play to its strengths.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and without a placing to his name in recent outings, Zephron at least has experience of today's trip and conditions, though 75 days off and a stiff 129 lb from stall 19 make this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Cannonball Queen
runners_data.note: Fading-in-finish flag, four consecutive finishes outside the first 12, and a sim-going record of 6 from 8 with no wins on Good — Ben Coen's booking is the one positive, but the overall profile makes a challenge from the back of this field very unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 17 of 20 on our figures, Cannonball Queen makes little appeal, though a fourth last time out at least shows some improvement and she has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Duchess Anne
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a placed record on Good ground and a second place over 10f recently in her favour; Gary Carroll rides and she has run competitively at both 8f and 10f, making her one of the more credible outsiders if traffic clears.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked well down the field on our figures, Duchess Anne faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a second last time out offers a sliver of encouragement; the 39-day gap is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Spiritofthedawn
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with only three career runs, all finishing 11th, last seen 120 days ago — the headgear flag (hg:t) and complete lack of any competitive form make this an extremely difficult task in a 20-runner handicap on debut from a break.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Spiritofthedawn faces a stiff task here; 120 days off the track adds a fitness query, though she has run over today's trip and a return to form cannot be entirely ruled out.

runners_data.name: Yorkshire Myth
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a best effort of second on Tapeta/Standard going; all five recent runs are on artificial surfaces, and Good turf at Navan is a clear unknown — the 82-day absence and blindfold flag (hg:b) add further doubt.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Yorkshire Myth has been unplaced in both recent outings and returns after 82 days off carrying 124 lb from stall 13; experience over today's trip and going offers slim consolation.

runners_data.name: Marambo
runners_data.note: The second prominent-profile horse in the race who could attach to Land Of The Giants early; however, three consecutive last-place finishes at this course on Good ground and a reserve jockey booking reduce confidence significantly despite the tactical position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and unplaced in three on the bounce, Marambo faces a stiff ask carrying 137 lb from stall 10, though he has run over today's trip and going before and our rating nudges above his official mark, suggesting a shade more ability than the bare form shows.

runners_data.name: Plastic Paddy
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type who has been running over extreme distances (16-24f) and whose only recent 8f run produced 14th place; the reserve jockey, fading flag, and complete mismatch of distance profile make this an outsider of outsiders.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 18th of 20 on our figures, Plastic Paddy faces a stiff task despite having run over today's trip and going before; carrying 122 lb from stall 14, there is little in the recent form to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: I'm Spartacus
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose entire career has been run over 5f and 6f — a mile is well beyond anything in the form book, and despite running just four days ago its distance profile is a fundamental mismatch; style fit 0.93 reflects its displacement in the map.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and back just four days later, I'm Spartacus faces a stiff ask from stall 15 carrying 134 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and our rating of 58 suggests a shade more ability than his mark of 52 implies.

races.paceDynamic: Land Of The Giants is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 20-runner field and, crucially, faces no meaningful pace pressure — Marambo is the only other prominent-profile runner and is unlikely to force a contest for the lead. With a single horse dictating from the front on Good ground over a flat Navan mile, the tempo will be sustainable rather than searching, creating a straightforward gallop that allows Land Of The Giants to control fractions and conserve energy into the straight. The field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up horses, but the going report confirms consistent Good ground throughout the card, meaning closers have a genuine surface to work with if they can find clear runs through what will be a congested midfield group. However, the vast majority of runners tagged [REDISTRIBUTED] — including Virgil Tibbs, Giselles Defence, I'm Spartacus, Dress Dance, Whosethebestboy, Chou Chou, Cannonball Queen, Duchess Anne and others — are true hold-up types who have been displaced to midfield on the map simply because the rear of the field cannot accommodate them all; most will not secure their natural position and will race compressed together, making run-finding difficult late. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape, with one uncontested pace-setter and a bunched midfield, favours horses who can sit prominently just behind Land Of The Giants in the slipstream or break early from midfield, rather than the deep hold-up horses who will face traffic problems in a wall of runners.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Land Of The Giants dictates a comfortable fractions-controlled pace and the congested midfield cannot produce a clean late challenge.
scenarios.body: Land Of The Giants sets an uncontested rhythm and, with nothing to pressure it, can extend its lead or at least hold on through the final furlong on ground that suits; Marambo, tracking close throughout, is best placed of all runners to pounce if the leader ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Clear Out
scenarios.trigger: If Land Of The Giants and Marambo stride clear together at a brisk enough tempo that the hold-up pack is strung out and cannot close.
scenarios.body: The two prominent-profile horses race close to the pace and effectively run the field ragged, with the final outcome between themselves; hold-up horses are caught in traffic too far back to mount a meaningful challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Thread Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just sharp enough to expose the prominent horses in the final furlong and one or two hold-up horses find a clear passage through the congested pack.
scenarios.body: Dinamine, who has proven Good-ground form at the trip and a recent win over this distance, or Perfect Judgement, who ran second over 10f recently, could thread late if the gaps appear; the scenario requires a clean run which is far from guaranteed given how many true hold-up types are compacted into the same space.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely in the straight and a single hold-up horse finds daylight before the rest of the tightly bunched group can respond.
scenarios.body: With so many horses racing out of their natural role and compressed together, the rare runner who secures an early gap on the outside could steal the race before rivals realise; Duchess Anne, who has placed over this distance on Good, and Chou Chou, whose last run produced a placed effort, are the likeliest beneficiaries of such a chaotic scenario.

watchPoints.text: Land Of The Giants is the only confirmed front-runner in a 20-horse field — if it quickens even modestly from the front, the congested hold-up pack behind it may simply never get close enough to challenge.

Dinamine (Wesley Joyce, 3lb claim) is the most dangerous closer in the race — watch for Joyce to track the pace from a handy hold-up position; a clean run could see this horse sprint home if the tempo is honest enough to catch the leader.

Marambo's reserve jockey booking is a significant unknown — if a named jockey takes over, reassess its chance as the second prominent horse who could make the running a genuine two-horse affair from the front.

With 14 or more horses effectively bunched in the middle of the field, traffic and interference in the straight are a near-certainty — horses drawn wide or with jockeys who commit early to an outside run (Carroll on Duchess Anne, Keane on Chou Chou) are most likely to avoid the worst of it.
The going report confirms Good ground has been consistent throughout the entire Navan card for all distances — no hidden soft patches or drying bias to factor in for this race specifically.

races.name: Navan Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Concert Party
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse for Hogan/Sheridan combination but form figures on Good ground are poor (six runs, no wins or places in similar conditions) and over a mile she has not threatened competitively; the slow pace and large field are double-edged — she won't be far enough back to get a true test.
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of the weights on our rating and carrying 142 lb from stall nine, Concert Party has run over today's trip and going and is fitter for a run 15 days ago — though winless in her last five starts, that form makes the risk plain.

runners_data.name: Moyassr
runners_data.note: Apprentice Sam Coen takes the ride for McGuinness who has had three runners in the past fortnight; one win and one place on Good ground across eight runs gives him some claim, and at 1m he has placed recently — a genuine midfield grinder who could run into a place at a decent price.
runners_data.comment: Moyassr returns just 15 days after his last start in fine fitness, and his experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset carrying 142 lb from stall seven; a winner in recent starts, though his last three have been below that level.

runners_data.name: Usuario Amigo
runners_data.note: Consistent in terms of position (regularly hits the frame in terms of running position) but form figures read 0-0-9-7-0 in similar going at this trip and he has not won in a long time; O'Brien's yard has had minimal firepower over this span and the 39-day break is a slight query.
runners_data.comment: Rated 66 and ranked second of 20 runners, Usuario Amigo brings distance and going experience to the table and returns on a workable 39-day break, but he is winless in his last six starts and that persistent out-of-the-frame form is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Suerte
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type for Lavery/Colgan who has been active (8 days since last run) but has failed to win or place in nine Good-ground appearances — the headgear (tongue tie) has not unlocked better form and a moderate pace over 1m is unlikely to suit her finishing style.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and drawn in stall 20, Suerte faces an uphill task, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick eight-day turnaround that suggests connections are hopeful.

runners_data.name: Distillate
runners_data.note: McGuinness runner who is a natural hold-up horse in profile, though the field's density means he will likely end up nearer midfield than his preferred rear position, tempering confidence; the switch to Good turf (most of his form has come on Standside/Heavy) and a blank win record in similar conditions further limits his appeal.
runners_data.comment: Distillate has run over today's trip and going, and a second five starts back shows she can threaten, yet she has been winless in recent starts and was brought down last time — the 135 lb burden from stall 11 adds further pressure on a mare needing things to fall right.

runners_data.name: Genuine Jim
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-setter and will face zero pace pressure, which keeps his chances alive despite poor recent form (0-0-0-0 in last four) — Burns' yard shows no recent record in the book and 76 days off is a concern, but he controls every aspect of the race shape and cannot be dismissed entirely.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and drawn in stall 17, Genuine Jim at least has experience of today's distance and going, and a speed rating of 65 suggests latent ability that his recent unplaced efforts have not reflected — though 76 days off the track is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Micasso
runners_data.note: Kinsella's four-year-old has winning form on Good going (won at 8f on Good) and another second in similar conditions — his true style is hold-up but the scale of redistribution in this field means he will likely race closer to midfield than usual, which on a flat mile with a soft pace is arguably not a disadvantage; Seamie Heffernan is a strong jockey booking.
runners_data.comment: Micasso won three starts back but has been unplaced either side of that success, leaving him with a mixed recent profile; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 133 lb from stall 3, and his rating of 50 suggests he faces a stiff task against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Thompson Gunner
runners_data.note: Colin Keane is a significant booking for Hughes' five-year-old, who has placed at 1m on Good ground and has shown consistency in prominent positions; headgear (tongue tie, blinkers) applied and the 19-day turnaround looks fine — this horse's natural style is ideally matched to the predicted race shape.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back gives Thompson Gunner a recent placed effort to cling to, but a fifth last time out and patchy form in between temper expectations; he has run over today's distance and going, and a 9 lb pull on our rating over his official mark offers mild encouragement.

runners_data.name: Make The Tide
runners_data.note: McCreery's three-year-old has a flag for fading in the finish, and form on Good going at 8f is limited (three runs, no places); W J Lee is a reliable partner but the horse's pattern of weakening inside the last furlong is a clear concern in a race where the finish could be a sprint.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Make The Tide has nonetheless shown some consistency in mid-division, and has run over today's trip and going before; 132 lb from stall 13 is no help, though her rating of 57 suggests she retains a little more ability than her recent efforts imply.

runners_data.name: Onyeisi
runners_data.note: Thornton's three-year-old has been running over further (10-13f) and drops back to 1m here, which may or may not suit — his best finish was a 4th at 10f on Good; Jack Cleary takes the 5lb claim but the horse's form cycle has not produced a placing on Good ground in six attempts.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Onyeisi's best recent effort was a fourth four starts back, though an unplaced run last time and a stall 19 draw give pause; experience over today's trip and going, plus a rating of 56, keep him in the mix at a competitive weight of 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Pettus Bridge
runners_data.note: Foster's four-year-old is flagged as a fade type with four Good-ground runs showing no wins or places; the fades-in-finish pattern is a concern if the race develops as a sprint from the front, and the short turnaround (8 days) adds a question mark.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 19 of 20 on our figures, Pettus Bridge faces a stiff ask here; consecutive ninths and a slip leave him hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip and going and arrives fit enough on just eight days' rest.

runners_data.name: Aghadrum Boy
runners_data.note: Murphy's three-year-old has only three career runs (4-8-12) and is a natural hold-up type pushed toward midfield on the map due to the congested rear; the fade flag is significant in a race with a modest pace, and experience at this trip and in a 20-runner field is limited.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, Aghadrum Boy has run over today's trip and going before, and 13 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; a rating of 55 offers modest encouragement, though recent form — unplaced latest and eighth the time before — makes improvement essential from stall eight off 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Pinball Wizard
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has shown his best form on Good ground with two places in similar conditions across ten runs — he is a natural hold-up type operating here from a midfield mapping position due to field size; McConnell's yard has been active (4/27 runners in 14 days) and the 62-day break is the main concern.
runners_data.comment: Pinball Wizard has run over today's trip and going before, yet his recent form reads poorly — winless in his last five starts with a string of unplaced efforts and a pair of sevenths — and 62 days off the track adds a fitness query, though a mark of 47 leaves room for improvement.

runners_data.name: Chant d'Or
runners_data.note: McLoughlin's four-year-old returns from a 316-day absence — an enormous layoff that is a major flag regardless of any other factor — and has only one Good-ground run to reference; the fade pattern and blinkers headgear suggest a horse still finding its level, and this return looks like a fitness run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and absent for 316 days, Chant d'Or faces a steep ask returning from a lengthy layoff; rated just 32 on our figures and ranked last of 20, he has experience of today's trip and conditions but little else to commend him here.

runners_data.name: Winston's Promise
runners_data.note: Cusack's three-year-old has shown 8th-8th finishes at 7-8f on Good, suggesting a horse who runs on without threatening; the fade flag, a pattern of finishing mid-pack at best, and redistribution away from the rear all make this a tough assignment in a 20-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 16 of 20 on our figures, Winston's Promise has shown little in recent outings, with consecutive eighths and two unplaced efforts his recent calling card; experience over today's trip and going is about the best that can be said for him here.

runners_data.name: Tariff
runners_data.note: Maxwell's three-year-old has a fade flag and poor Good-ground form (two runs in similar conditions, no places); drops from a 39-day break and has been tried in headgear historically — a horse who regularly runs out of gear in the closing stages at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a string of mid-field and tail-end finishes, Tariff is hard to fancy from stall 18 carrying 122 lb, and our figures rank him fifteenth of twenty — though he does have experience over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Darwin's Angel
runners_data.note: Duffy's three-year-old is a natural hold-up type shown in midfield due to field congestion; form figures over 7-11f on Good ground are consistently poor (12th, 13th, 12th, 13th) — the headgear (pads) has not changed the pattern and this looks a difficult race on any reading.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and rated just 40 officially, Darwin's Angel nevertheless holds a nine-pound edge over her official mark on our rating, and she has run over today's distance and going before; 39 days between runs and stall five round out a picture of modest prospects with a sliver of upside.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: Mulvany's three-year-old has raced to two places on Good ground in nine attempts and has the headgear (tongue tie); no jockey listed in the data is a minor flag but the horse's prominent style fits the predicted race shape — has run 2nd at 10f on Good going which is relevant recent evidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and unplaced most recently, Borora Aura does at least have experience over today's distance and going, but stepping out of stall two carrying 128 lb, she looks to have plenty to find on her rating of 51 in a 20-runner field.

runners_data.name: Hastily
runners_data.note: McGuinness's seven-year-old has one win in 15 Good-ground appearances and the fade flag is present; form at 8f on Good is weak (13th, 15th recent), no jockey confirmed, and the 40-day break combined with the pattern of finishing tailed off makes this a very outside contender.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a string of unplaced efforts and a ranking of 18th of 20 on our figures, Hastily is hard to fancy here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 40-day break.

runners_data.name: Bang Po
runners_data.note: McAteer's six-year-old has a fade flag and has been running over much longer trips (13-14f) — dropping back to 1m is a significant change in trip that is unlikely to suit a horse whose form at this distance on Good ground reads 11th; no jockey confirmed and the 8-day turnaround after a poor run adds little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 17th of 20 on our figures, Bang Po is hard to fancy despite a quick turnaround of eight days and experience over today's trip and going; stall one is his sole neutral consolation.

races.paceDynamic: Genuine Jim is the sole confirmed front runner in a 20-runner field and, critically, faces no meaningful pressure for the lead — Thompson Gunner, Borora Aura and Pettus Bridge are the prominent types most likely to slot in just behind, but none is a natural pace-setter who will force a genuine battle for the lead. With a single, uncontested pace-setter over a flat Navan mile in Good conditions, the tempo will be controlled and sustainable rather than hot, meaning the race will not string out early and there will be a significant bunch travelling together through the middle stages. That compressed shape — moderate gallop, large field, one-mile trip — historically benefits horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace and produce a turn-of-foot in the straight, rather than deep closers who need strong pace to get competitive. The field holds materially more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Distillate, Aghadrum Boy, Micasso, Pinball Wizard, Chant d'Or and several others are genuine hold-up horses in profile but are mapped to midfield precisely because they cannot all settle at the back of a 20-runner field, and those who do end up at the rear will find a moderate pace wholly against them. **Tactical verdict: prominent runners and those able to travel in the first half-dozen, who carry a finishing kick under a patient but not too-far-back ride, are best placed in this race shape.**

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Genuine Jim Controls Softly
scenarios.trigger: If Genuine Jim sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent trio track smoothly without injecting pressure.
scenarios.body: Genuine Jim dictates from the front at a pace that suits himself and the horses just behind him, and the race turns into a sprint for home from the two-furlong pole; horses racing within two to four lengths of the leader from the outset are optimally positioned as there is no gap to close from the rear. Thompson Gunner and Borora Aura, tracking close throughout, are ideally profiled — a genuine turn of foot at the business end rewards those who have conserved energy in a handy berth.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger than expected and a late run from a genuinely well-positioned midfield horse catches the leader napping.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting in the centre of the 20-runner pack travels smoothly and, once competitive racing begins entering the straight, produces a sustained finish on a field that has burned marginally more gas up front than anticipated; Micasso, who has winning form on Good ground over this trip and is shown in midfield (though a natural hold-up type operating in a better position than usual), or Moyassr could be the beneficiary. The key requirement is that the middle group remains compact and that at least one horse has the class or recent form to peel off and sustain a run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Pinched Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Genuine Jim is allowed an entirely uncontested lead and the pack behind fails to organise a coherent response until too late.
scenarios.body: Genuine Jim, completely untroubled on the front end, steals a decisive advantage turning for home before the chasing pack realises the margin; in a field this large with a slow-tempo scenario, coordination from the pursuing group can break down and the leader simply gallops clear. This scenario directly rewards front-running tactics and punishes both midfield and rear-positioned horses whose redistribution away from the back means they are not close enough to strike quickly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough — perhaps from a prominent horse pressing Genuine Jim — to produce an honestly-run mile that suits deep closers.
scenarios.body: A surprise injection of pace from one of the prominent types turns this into a truly-run race and strings the field out, giving genuine hold-up horses a pace to chase down; however, this scenario is the least likely given only one confirmed front runner and a field where the supposed closers are largely redistributed types who will not be far enough back to benefit. If it does materialise, horses with the most authentic hold-up profiles — Concert Party or Suerte — could theoretically finish best of all, but their form figures on Good ground offer limited encouragement.

watchPoints.text: Watch Thompson Gunner's early positioning — if Colin Keane slots him second or third behind Genuine Jim from the outset, he is the horse best placed to capitalise on a steadily-run mile and an unanswered front runner.

Genuine Jim's lead margin at the two-furlong pole is critical — if uncontested, Burns may have engineered a sizable advantage before the field realises, making the front-runner scenario far more dangerous than his poor recent form suggests.
