Monitor Micasso's draw and early manoeuvring — Seamie Heffernan's presence means the horse will be ridden aggressively into a better position than his natural hold

races.name: Navan Racing Festival 14th & 15th November Handicap

runners_data.name: Daler
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist trained by G M Lyons who won over 9f on Soft last time and has solid Good-ground form; Gary Carroll rides, and the step back to a strongly-run 1m suits his profile well with cheekpieces and tongue-tie fitted.
runners_data.comment: Daler shaped with promise when second three starts back and a winner four starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going keeps him very much in contention off a mark of 82; the worry is that fifth last time out leaves fitness from a 30-day absence to prove.

runners_data.name: Hygge
runners_data.note: Ran over 1m on Soft last time but has two wins on Good going at 8f; Declan McDonogh takes over for Gordon Elliott and a prominent draw from a small recent sample makes this one to treat with respect if the pace sets things up.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 16 of 21 on our figures and the trainer is in a dire spell at 1/40 over the past fortnight, making him very hard to fancy despite a win two starts back; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 140 lb from stall 15 complete a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Frank Pickle
runners_data.note: Won last time at 1m on Good under Wayne Lordan; trainer Denise Foster has just one runner in the 14-day window, and the prominent style should allow him to sit just off the hot pace without burning energy unnecessarily.
runners_data.comment: Frank Pickle won two starts back but was well beaten on his latest outing 39 days ago, leaving fitness a mild query; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 139 lb from stall three, and our rating of 84 suggests a shade of unexploited potential.

runners_data.name: Harana
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes partners this Dermot Weld-trained 4yo who won a 10f race on Good and has placed twice at a mile; prominent style and strong trainer record at 2/20 in 14 days makes this a serious contender in a scenario where the pace collapses mid-race.
runners_data.comment: Harana boasts a win three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 86 suggesting she holds strong claims in this field; the risk is that back-to-back seventh and fifth placings in recent starts raise questions about whether she can recapture that form.

runners_data.name: Sonoran
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for G M Lyons on this hold-up type who has been running over further (10f) and not winning, but does have a place at 10f on Good; the compression back to 8f in a strong-pace race could unlock a finish.
runners_data.comment: Sonoran shaped with promise when third five starts back and arrives here fit on a 17-day turnaround, with experience over today's trip and going and an 87 rating that marks him out as a leading contender; the concern is he has been winless in his last six starts and must prove he can convert that latent ability.

runners_data.name: Exquisite Acclaim
runners_data.note: One of the confirmed front-runners, a 7yo wearing a visor, who has drawn sharp sectionals at 7f on Good; Sam Coen (5lb claimer) takes over and the step up to 8f looks a query, but the horse's primary role here is as a pace-maker rather than a winner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Exquisite Acclaim returns after 21 days with experience over today's distance and going in his favour, though a fourth last time out and just one placed effort before that suggest he remains one to treat with caution from stall 11 carrying 138 lb.

runners_data.name: Spodo Komodo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won at 6f on Soft; Seamie Heffernan rides, which gives the horse credibility, but recent form at 8f on Good is poor (two 10th-place finishes) and the extra ground looks a genuine stamina question.
runners_data.comment: Spodo Komodo has experience over today's trip and going and returns just 15 days after his last start, but two unplaced efforts in recent starts temper enthusiasm, and a hefty 137 lb is no help from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Marmeladova
runners_data.note: Strong record on Good going (12/13 sim-going runs) with two wins and five places; this 5yo hold-up filly won at 10f and placed at 12f, suggesting the 8f flat Navan mile is likely on the short side, though the pace scenario could suit.
runners_data.comment: Marmeladova has experience over today's trip and going, and a win four starts back offers a crumb of encouragement, but three winless efforts since — the most recent a fifth — suggest she faces a stiff task from draw 4 carrying 136 lb.

runners_data.name: Cala Bonita
runners_data.note: Prominent-running 4yo who won at 8f on Soft; Good-ground form is mixed but the horse has placed in decent handicaps and Matthew J Smith's stable is not firing (0/5 in 14 days), which tempers enthusiasm despite the tactical profile fitting.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 19 of 21 on our figures, Cala Bonita faces a stiff ask, and a ninth last time out does little to inspire confidence, though she did score two starts back and has experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Great Mover
runners_data.note: Third of the confirmed front-runners, an improving 4yo for Willie McCreery who has won over shorter; T14 of 5/13 is an excellent in-form trainer flag, and Paddy Harnett (3lb claimer) helps with weight, but burning energy fighting for the lead in a 21-runner field looks his undoing.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Great Mover nevertheless has experience over today's trip and going, and a speed rating of 85 offers some encouragement; drawn 19 and carrying 134 lb, she returns after 17 days and faces a stiff task breaking that duck.

runners_data.name: Morehampton
runners_data.note: Ran just 2 days ago — extremely short turnaround for a 3yo — and J P Murtagh's runner has Good-ground placed form at 7-8f; the freshness concern is significant and Patrick McGettigan (5lb claimer) will need to find a clean run from a big field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Morehampton has placed in his two most recent outings and has experience over today's trip and conditions, but a run just two days ago and a trainer strike-rate of just 3% in the past fortnight give pause from stall 20 carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: No More Porter
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type with five places at 8f on Good and no wins from 7 sim-going runs; the 8yo Adam Caffrey partner is reliable rather than progressive but a truly run mile right in his wheelhouse could deliver a place at minimum.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, No More Porter nonetheless brings a degree of encouragement through third and second finishes in recent outings, and has run over today's trip and going before; the 134 lb burden, however, could prove the stiffest test here.

runners_data.name: Zaraahmando
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides, and the 4yo boasts an outstanding Good-ground record (12/15 sim-going runs, 2 wins, 6 places); all recent form is at 8f and the prominent-style profile places him just off the pace — a genuinely underrated contender.
runners_data.comment: Zaraahmando has been consistently placed in recent starts — second last time out and third three starts back — yet remains winless in his last six, which is the obvious concern. A trainer firing at 29% and experience over today's trip and going give him every chance from stall nine carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Anvika
runners_data.note: Sheila Lavery's 5yo has a strong record placing on Good ground (0W4P sim-going) and naturally wants to come from behind; shunted into a mapped midfield slot because the rear is overcrowded, meaning she is likely to race closer than ideal and the style fit is compromised (STYLE_FIT=0.91).
runners_data.comment: Placed third in two of her last six starts but winless in that recent spell, Anvika has experience of today's trip and going, though 55 days off and 133 lb from stall 14 are factors to weigh against a market position that leaves little margin for error.

runners_data.name: Halon Bay
runners_data.note: Ciaran Murphy's 3yo won at 7f on Good and placed at 8f, but has been off 75 days and the sim-going sample is thin (1/4); Ben Coen takes over and the prominent style could suit if the horse returns in peak condition after the break.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well adrift of the field on our figures, Halon Bay has been off 75 days and faces a stiff task from stall 21 carrying 131 lb, though he does bring winning form from his last four starts and has experience over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Only One Scobie
runners_data.note: Has won at 8f on both Good and Heavy, but a finishing-fade flag is noted and two recent 13th-place finishes on Good are hard to ignore; Leigh Roche partners for Paul Flynn and the tendency to stop late is a significant concern in a strongly-run race.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Only One Scobie faces a stiff ask off 131 lb from stall 10, and two unplaced efforts in his last three starts do little to inspire confidence, though he has won twice in recent starts and has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Felix Somary
runners_data.note: John O'Donoghue's 3yo has placed twice at 8-10f on Good wearing a visor; Rory Mulligan (5lb claimer) rides, and the recent form (0-3-3) suggests a horse capable of filling places rather than winning, sitting in a prominent position without the finishing gear to dominate.
runners_data.comment: Twice third in his last two starts, Felix Somary arrives here in reasonable nick after 31 days off and has run over today's trip and going before, but he remains winless in his last five starts and a mark of 75 with 130 lb to carry makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: Slight Of Foot
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type for R P Cody whose natural home is at the rear of the field; pushed into a mapped midfield slot by the sheer number of hold-up horses in the race (STYLE_FIT=0.91), meaning it is unlikely to get the clean passage it needs to deliver its finishing kick.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 18th of 21 on our figures, Slight Of Foot faces a stiff task here, though third last time out offers a crumb of comfort and he has run over today's trip and going before, drawing stall one carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Expound
runners_data.note: Fourth pace-setter in this field and a 7yo wearing tongue-tie and cheekpieces; Denis Hogan has 2/26 runners in 14 days and Expound's recent form shows finishes of 7th, 4th, 14th — it is likely to contribute to a fast early gallop before fading and has no realistic winning claim.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 15th of 21 on our figures, Expound faces a stiff ask here; he does have experience over today's trip and going, and 18 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, but the overall profile makes him difficult to fancy.

runners_data.name: Colpe Cross
runners_data.note: Off 397 days, the longest absence in the field by a distance, with only three career runs in the data; the unknown factor is enormous and Miss Natalia Lupini's runner has no sim-going wins — treat as an each-way outsider at best until fitness is established.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and absent for 397 days, Colpe Cross nonetheless catches the eye on her overall profile — a second two starts back on today's going hints at conditions suiting, and our rating of 89 makes her a lively pick from stall seven carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Dream Legend
runners_data.note: Has won at 8f on both Good and Soft, but the finishing-fade flag and the redistribution from its natural hold-up position tell the real story; the 3yo for E D Delany is being mapped to midfield only because the rear is saturated, and it is unlikely to deliver its natural style in this race shape (STYLE_FIT=0.92).
runners_data.comment: Dream Legend has won twice in his last five starts, with a victory last time out and a third two starts back, but ranked last on our figures and returning from 62 days off, he is hard to fancy at the weights from stall 17.

races.paceDynamic: Exquisite Acclaim, Spodo Komodo, and Great Mover are all confirmed front-runners in a 21-runner field over a flat Navan mile on Good ground, virtually guaranteeing a strong, pressured gallop from the outset with no prospect of a dawdle. Expound adds a fourth pace element, meaning the leaders will burn each other up through the early and middle sections, almost certainly setting things up for those racing off a strong tempo rather than those attempting to dictate. The hold-up contingent — Daler, Sonoran, Marmeladova, and No More Porter — are the profiles who will benefit most from a truly run race, as stamina and sustained finishing power will be at a premium over this flat mile. Anvika, Slight Of Foot, and Dream Legend are genuine hold-up types pushed into a mapped midfield position because the rear of this field is oversupplied with closers; they are unlikely to secure their natural position and their effectiveness in the closing stages should be discounted accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Closers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the four front-runners burn each other out setting a genuine gallop, freeing up the hold-up horses to sweep through late.
scenarios.body: The relentless early pace from Exquisite Acclaim, Spodo Komodo, Great Mover and Expound will leave the leaders spent in the final two furlongs, gifting the closers a collapsing target on the flat Navan mile. Daler, Marmeladova and No More Porter are all proven on Good ground at this sort of trip and are best equipped to finish strongly off a strong pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the early speed fizzles rather than burns — one front-runner dominates and the others capitulate — leaving a prominent racer to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Hygge or Harana, both sitting a couple of lengths off the burning pace without getting involved in the early war, would be ideally positioned to pounce as the leaders crack in the final quarter-mile. Both have course-relevant form on Good ground and enough class to capitalise if the pace scenario delivers a midrace vacuum.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three principal front-runners — most likely Spodo Komodo — seizes a clear early lead and is allowed to dictate at a more controlled tempo despite the presence of rivals.
scenarios.body: In a big field with 21 runners, positional chaos at the start can allow one horse to slip the field and build a lead that proves unassailable on the flat Navan circuit where holding a rail position is an advantage. Spodo Komodo has won over shorter while showing tactical speed and could exploit a fractious early break if rivals check each other.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but the true closers get shuffled back further than ideal, allowing a well-placed midfield horse to thread through for a decisive run.
scenarios.body: Zaraahmando has an excellent record on Good ground at this sort of trip and profiles as a horse that can sit mid-pack without being caught wide, while Cala Bonita and Felix Somary both have the tactical flexibility to travel in a handy position without being fully exposed to the pace. These types benefit if the closers are blocked or checked, presenting a gap through the middle.

watchPoints.text: Exquisite Acclaim, Spodo Komodo and Great Mover will fight for the lead from the outset in a 21-runner field — watch for a contested, physical battle for the front rail inside the first two furlongs that could cause checked runs and interference throughout the field.

Daler and No More Porter are both confirmed hold-up horses who will need to find daylight through a big field in the closing stages — watch for traffic problems in the straight as the pace collapses and the field fans wide.
Morehampton ran just two days ago and is the freshness concern of the race — watch for any signs of sluggishness or flatness early as the 3yo attempts to back up on a very tight turnaround.

Anvika, Slight Of Foot and Dream Legend are all natural closers mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear — watch to see whether any of them can drop back to their true position at the start or whether they are forced to race prominently against their instincts.

Colpe Cross returns after 397 days off and has no public gallop or trial evidence in the data — watch for betting market signals in the final hour before the race as the key indicator of whether the stable believes this horse is ready to run a big race first time back.

races.name: Racing Again This Saturday Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: Pampar Lady
runners_data.note: Older, experienced hold-up performer whose recent form shows a placed effort at 2m and consistent Good-ground running; the drop back to 1m2f may not fully suit a horse who stays further, and her natural rear-of-field style risks being swamped in a 23-runner bunched finish.

runners_data.name: Queen Of Chenab
runners_data.note: Returns from a 615-day absence with a tendency to fade in the finish, making her deeply vulnerable on return to action; the layoff alone is a severe concern regardless of her previous form, and her hold-up style does nothing to mitigate the traffic dangers in this field.

runners_data.name: Bang Bang
runners_data.note: Placed twice at this sort of trip and cost-effective form-wise, but a natural hold-up type pushed into a midfield map slot because the rear is overcrowded; the blinkers suggest she needs motivation, and her style-fit discount (0.92) tempers confidence that she can reproduce her best in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Chosen One
runners_data.note: Has a placed run over 10f on Good ground and wears a tongue-tie, but Donnacha O'Brien's charge is a genuine closer whose redistribution to midfield reflects the congested field rather than her true racing style; her best chance arrives only if the pace is strong enough to create daylight through a 23-runner field.

runners_data.name: Estrallita
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just one run, finishing sixth over 8f on Good ground; unknown style makes her a complete wildcard, and with Jack Davison's yard at 0/4 in the 14-day window there is no support from trainer form to elevate confidence.

runners_data.name: Fairylike
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's yard is ticking along (7/45 T14) and this filly showed a promising fourth over 10f on Good ground last time out; her prominent style is ideally suited to tracking Mawhibah into the straight, making her one of the most tactically well-positioned runners in the field.

runners_data.name: Gentle Soda
runners_data.note: Trainer McNamara has a quiet recent strike-rate (0/14 T14) and this filly finished a distant 12th on debut over 8f; a natural hold-up type shuffled into midfield only because the rear is saturated, she fades in the finish and the redistribution discount (0.90) reflects genuine concern about her chance.

runners_data.name: Hey Stella
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride on this G M Lyons filly who placed third over 1m2f on Good ground — the only runner in this field with a top-three finish at this exact trip and going combination; unknown style is the caveat but Keane will find her the best position available.

runners_data.name: Lamar Valley
runners_data.note: Two unplaced efforts on Good ground, both in sprinting or shorter trips (8f, 10f), and stepping up to 1m2f for the first time; hold-up style with no strong form evidence to recommend her at this distance.

runners_data.name: Mawhibah
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner, trained by Joseph Patrick O'Brien who is in excellent form (12/79 T14); has placed twice over 12f on Good ground and should be fully at home on this track and trip, and her ability to dictate uncontested is the defining tactical fact of this race.

runners_data.name: Near Perfection
runners_data.note: 130-day absence for Donnacha O'Brien and only one run to reference (fifth over 12f on Good); the layoff is a genuine concern for a horse with unknown style beyond debut, and the tongue-tie is noted but offers insufficient evidence of its effect.

runners_data.name: Orphanina
runners_data.note: Two very poor finishes (9th, 10th) over shorter trips on Good ground, returning on eight days' rest which is an unusually quick turnaround; the fade-in-finish flag and hold-up style leave her with little hope in this large, congested field.

runners_data.name: Peshwari Nan
runners_data.note: Three runs all ending in double-figure finishes, including 12ths on two occasions; Siobhan Rutledge rides but the form and the fade-in-finish flag make this hold-up type deeply unconvincing, and only one of her three runs was on comparable going.

runners_data.name: Saxony Charms
runners_data.note: Three consistent fifths and a third — all on Good ground over 10f — give her the most reliable form profile among the prominent runners; the blinkers likely sharpen her focus and Augustus Oliver's yard, while quiet recently, has a filly who should be competitive racing prominently off Mawhibah's pace.

runners_data.name: Serendipia
runners_data.note: Five runs all on Good ground, placed twice, and trained by W McCreery who is on a decent run (5/13 T14); a natural closer whose true rear-of-field style is displaced by the congested field but she has the best going-form base among the redistributed hold-up types and is the one most likely to make it work if gaps appear.

runners_data.name: Shanala
runners_data.note: John Murtagh's filly returns after 90 days off with two unplaced efforts at 10f; prominent style suits her tactically and she will look to track Mawhibah, but the layoff is a moderate concern and the form does not inspire confidence that she can win even if positioned well.

runners_data.name: Socratea
runners_data.note: Returned a seventh on debut at 8f for McCreery; the stable runs two today (Serendipia is the more fancied entrant) and Socratea's hold-up style and single uninspiring run give her limited claim in a 23-runner field at an extended trip.

runners_data.name: Sunatia
runners_data.note: Dermot Weld's filly placed second over 9f on Good ground on debut and Chris Hayes rides; the prominent style means she will naturally sit close to Mawhibah and that placed run suggests she handles Good ground and the step to 1m2f could unlock improvement given her pedigree context.

runners_data.name: Susie's Angel
runners_data.note: A single sixth over 7f on Good ground with a 7lb claimer aboard for Mark Fahey; unknown style, minimal form, and a low-profile yard (0/5 T14) — little to recommend her in a field of this size.

runners_data.name: Ventriloquist
runners_data.note: John McConnell's second string after a 90-day absence; her only run produced an 11th on Soft, which is a different surface profile, and the fade-in-finish flag combined with the lengthy break makes her a very difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Vivere A Colori
runners_data.note: Debutante for Mrs John Harrington whose yard has been ticking over (2/35 T14); unknown style and no race experience mean she is a complete unknown, though Harrington is capable of producing a sharp first-runner and Nathan Crosse's booking is noted.

runners_data.name: What Do You Say
runners_data.note: Second runner for Augustus Oliver (alongside Saxony Charms) on debut with an unknown style; no evidence to assess and the trainer's recent figures (0/14 T14) offer no support — purely speculative.

runners_data.name: Windbourne
runners_data.note: Debutante for Patrick Foley (0/7 T14) with Luke McAteer taking the ride; unknown style and no form to assess, with the trainer's blank 14-day record doing nothing to encourage confidence in a market-leading position.

races.paceDynamic: Mawhibah is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 23-runner maiden and, critically, faces no realistic pace pressure from any other genuine lead horse — she can dictate entirely on her own terms from flag to finish at Navan's 1m2f trip on good ground. Fairylike, Saxony Charms, Shanala and Sunatia will push forward from prominent positions and may apply some early pressure, but none are habitual leaders, so Mawhibah should find a comfortable rhythm and control the tempo without being burned up. The field contains a significant surplus of hold-up types — Gentle Soda, Serendipia, Bang Bang and Chosen One are all genuine closers who have been redistributed into the midfield map position simply because there is no physical room for them all to race from the rear in a 23-runner field, and they are unlikely to get their natural late-running role. In a large-field maiden with a single uncontested front-runner setting a sustainable gallop on good ground over 1m2f, the race shape favours prominent racers who can track the leader without expending energy early and then quicken into the straight, rather than true closers who will face traffic and distance issues in a compressed bunched field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mawhibah Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Mawhibah dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and kicks clear before the field can organise a challenge.
scenarios.body: Mawhibah trots along in front at her own pace, the prominent holders settle nicely in behind without crowding her, and the large field bunches causing chaos for any late movers; she simply extends her lead turning in and holds on. Prominent-tracking types who sit just off her and avoid the traffic melee benefit most, with Fairylike and Saxony Charms ideally placed to pick up the scraps.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Swamp Her
scenarios.trigger: If the pack of prominent types — Fairylike, Saxony Charms, Shanala, Sunatia — collectively press Mawhibah through the middle stages and she weakens in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Mawhibah is not outpaced early but the four prominent horses collectively apply enough sustained pressure that she ties up entering the final two furlongs, leaving the trailing pack of prominent stalkers to battle it out. Horses who settled just off the pace and travel well within themselves — Fairylike and Sunatia, both trained by handlers with strong current strike-rates — are best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves stronger than expected and a true closer manages to thread through the large field to deliver a late run.
scenarios.body: The redistributed closers — Serendipia and Bang Bang — would need genuine luck in running through a 23-runner field plus a strong pace that strings the field out; both carry style-fit discounts precisely because they cannot count on getting a clear passage or their true hold-up role in this race shape. Serendipia has the most consistent form profile among the closers with five good-ground runs to reference, and Bang Bang stepped up over this sort of trip last time, making them the most credible beneficiaries if the scenario clicks.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutantes Cause Shock
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unraced or lightly raced unknown-style fillies produces a natural front-running or prominent debut and catches the field flat-footed.
scenarios.body: With Vivere A Colori, What Do You Say and Windbourne all making debuts with unknown styles, any one of them could turn out to be a natural front-runner or prominent type who slots in behind Mawhibah unnoticed and outstays the field; Hey Stella showed a placed third effort at 1m2f on good ground and remains lightly raced with scope for improvement under Colin Keane. This scenario is low probability but the sheer size of the field and number of unknowns keeps it on the radar.

watchPoints.text: Mawhibah (J M Sheridan / J P O'Brien) has completely uncontested lead and a 12/79 14-day trainer strike-rate — if she settles at the front as expected she could prove very hard to peg back in the straight, making her the single most dangerous factor in shaping the race.

With 23 runners on the turn into Navan's straight, traffic could be severely problematic for the redistributed hold-up types — Serendipia, Bang Bang, Chosen One and Gentle Soda are all racing out of position and any one of them could cause or suffer significant interference.
